**Name of the Surah**

• It is called "An-Nazi'at" (Those who Pull Out), because it opens with Allah's oath by "An-Nazi'at," meaning the angels who pull out the souls of the children of Adam. This word does not occur in any other surah.

**Some of the Surah's Aims**

• Affirming the Resurrection and the Recompense through an oath, refuting the polytheists' doubt that the Resurrection could occur, and magnifying the Day of Resurrection and depicting the state of people on it.

**[The Tafsir]**

Allah the Exalted swears by the angels who pull out the souls of the disbelievers with severe force, and the angels who take the souls of the believers with ease and gentleness, and the angels who glide as they descend from the sky and ascend back to it, then the angels who race ahead and hasten to carry out Allah's command, then the angels who execute the command of their Lord in what has been entrusted to them of the affairs of the universe. -It is not permissible for a created being to swear by other than its Creator; whoever does so has committed shirk.- Surely the creatures will be resurrected and called to account, on the Day when the earth will be convulsed by the first blast, the blast of death, which will be followed by another blast for resurrection.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 79, verses 27–33:

Are you, O people, harder to create after death, or is the creation of the sky harder? He raised it above you like a building, and made its ceiling high in the air, without any flaw or fissure. He darkened its night by the setting of its sun, and brought forth its day by its rising. And the earth, after the creation of the sky, He spread out, placed in it its benefits, caused springs of water to gush forth from it, brought forth from it the pasture plants that are grazed, and fixed the mountains in it as pegs for it. God, glory be to Him, created all these blessings as a benefit for you and your livestock. Indeed, the re-creation of you on the Day of Resurrection is easier for God than the creation of these things, and everything is easy and simple for God.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 79, verses 42–46:

The disbelievers ask you, O Messenger, mockingly, about the time when the Hour (al-Sa'ah) that they are threatened with will arrive. You have no knowledge of it at all. Rather, the matter of it returns to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Your only task regarding the Hour is to warn those who fear it. It will be as if, on the day they see the Hour established, they had not remained in the worldly life except for an interval between midday and sunset, or between sunrise and midday, because of the terror of the Hour.
